newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps gives Double-B to Mexican bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps gives Double-B to Mexican bond issue.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Monday it assigned a Double-B foreign currency rating to the $1 billion global bond issue from Mexico.
The 10-year bonds have a 9.875 percent coupon.
Duff & Phelps said it has a positive view of Mexico's economy and credit standing, underpinning the rating.

"The Mexican government's commitment to tight monetary and fiscal policies has cause annual inflation to steadily decline from 52 percent in 1995 to 28 percent in 1996, while GDP (gross domestic product) growth picked up to about 3.7 percent in 1996," the firm said in a release.
Duff & Phelps said Mexico's ailing financial sector is still a concern but has benefited from improving fundamentals as well as a restructuring program.
